record.original_question: Are the only finite-type surfaces in the standard 3-sphere S^3 the minimal surfaces, the standard 2-spheres, and the products of two plane circles?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2. Minimal surfaces, standard 2-spheres and products of plane circles are the only finite type surfaces in S^3 (imbedded standardly in E^4).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^3 \subset \mathbb{E}^4$ denote the unit 3-sphere standardly embedded in Euclidean 4-space. For a closed surface $M$ smoothly immersed in $S^3 \subset \mathbb{E}^4$, regard the position vector $x : M \to \mathbb{E}^4$ component-wise as smooth functions on $M$, and let $\Delta$ be the Laplace–Beltrami operator of the induced Riemannian metric on $M$. The immersion is said to be of finite type if the position vector admits a finite spectral decomposition
$$x = x_0 + x_{t_1} + x_{t_2} + \cdots + x_{t_k},$$
where $x_0$ is a constant vector in $\mathbb{E}^4$ and each non-constant $\mathbb{E}^4$-valued function $x_{t_i}$ satisfies $\Delta x_{t_i} = \lambda_{t_i} x_{t_i}$ for some real eigenvalue $\lambda_{t_i}$, with $k$ finite.

Three families of surfaces in $S^3$ are known to be of finite type:
(i) minimal surfaces in $S^3$;
(ii) standard 2-spheres in $S^3$ (i.e., intersections of $S^3$ with affine hyperplanes of $\mathbb{E}^4$);
(iii) products of two plane circles, i.e., flat tori of the form $\{(r_1\cos\theta,\, r_1\sin\theta,\, r_2\cos\varphi,\, r_2\sin\varphi) : \theta,\varphi\in\mathbb{R}\}$ with $r_1^2+r_2^2=1$.

Question: Is every finite-type surface in $S^3$ (standardly embedded in $\mathbb{E}^4$) one of the surfaces in families (i), (ii), or (iii)?
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of finite-type surfaces in S^3 (in the sense of B.-Y. Chen's spectral decomposition) remains an active and open area of research. Surveys and recent papers on finite-type and finite Chen-type surfaces (e.g., works by Stamatakis–Al-Zoubi and subsequent literature) continue to treat the problem as unresolved, with results obtained only under additional restrictions (e.g., ruled, tubular, rotational, or factorable surfaces). No source confirming a full proof or counterexample to the conjecture was found.

status_evidence.title: On Surfaces of finite Chen-type
status_evidence.snippet: Up to now, the only known finite type surfaces in S^3 are minimal surfaces, standard 2-spheres and products of plane circles; the general classification problem remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The classification problem for finite-type surfaces in S^3 is still open.

status_evidence.title: On spectral decomposition of immersions of finite type
status_evidence.snippet: Studies finite-type immersions and their spectral decomposition; classification problems in low dimensions remain active.
status_evidence.claim: Finite-type classification problems are an active area without a complete answer.
